ExplanationA: Incorrect. The correct answer is B: White blood cells. White blood cells are central to immune defence against infections.
ExplanationB: Correct. White blood cells are central to immune defence against infections.
ExplanationC: Incorrect. The correct answer is B: White blood cells. White blood cells are central to immune defence against infections.
ExplanationD: Incorrect. The correct answer is B: White blood cells. White blood cells are central to immune defence against infections.

Question: The planet known as the Red Planet is:
ExplanationA: Incorrect. The correct answer is B: Mars. Mars is commonly called the Red Planet because of iron oxides on its surface.
ExplanationB: Correct. Mars is commonly called the Red Planet because of iron oxides on its surface.
ExplanationC: Incorrect. The correct answer is B: Mars. Mars is commonly called the Red Planet because of iron oxides on its surface.
ExplanationD: Incorrect. The correct answer is B: Mars. Mars is commonly called the Red Planet because of iron oxides on its surface.

Question: Electric resistance is measured in:
ExplanationA: Incorrect. The correct answer is C: Ohm. The ohm is the SI unit of electrical resistance.
ExplanationB: Incorrect. The correct answer is C: Ohm. The ohm is the SI unit of electrical resistance.
ExplanationC: Correct. The ohm is the SI unit of electrical resistance.
ExplanationD: Incorrect. The correct answer is C: Ohm. The ohm is the SI unit of electrical resistance.

Question: Approximately what is the speed of light in vacuum?
ExplanationA: 3 × 10^4 m/s is far below the speed of electromagnetic radiation in vacuum.
ExplanationB: 3 × 10^6 m/s is too small by about two orders of magnitude.
ExplanationC: Correct. The speed of light in vacuum is approximately 3 × 10^8 metres per second.
ExplanationD: 3 × 10^10 m/s is about one hundred times too large.

Question: Which type of lens converges parallel rays of light to a principal focus in air?
ExplanationA: A concave lens generally diverges parallel rays.
ExplanationB: Correct. A convex lens is a converging lens and brings parallel rays toward a principal focus.
ExplanationC: A plane glass slab may refract light but does not act as a converging lens with a principal focus.
ExplanationD: A cylindrical mirror is a reflecting surface, not the converging lens described.

Question: A transformer operates primarily on which physical principle?
ExplanationA: Correct. Transformers use changing magnetic flux and electromagnetic induction to transfer electrical energy between coils.
ExplanationB: The photoelectric effect concerns emission of electrons from materials exposed to suitable radiation.
ExplanationC: Radioactive decay is a nuclear process and is not the operating principle of a transformer.
ExplanationD: Electrolysis is a chemical process driven by electric current through an electrolyte.

Question: What is the common name of sodium hydrogen carbonate, NaHCO₃?
ExplanationA: Washing soda is sodium carbonate decahydrate, not sodium hydrogen carbonate.
ExplanationB: Correct. Sodium hydrogen carbonate is commonly called baking soda.
ExplanationC: Bleaching powder is a chlorine-containing compound used mainly for bleaching and disinfection.
ExplanationD: Plaster of Paris is calcium sulfate hemihydrate.

Question: In terms of electron transfer, oxidation is defined as:
ExplanationA: Gain of electrons is reduction, not oxidation.
ExplanationB: Correct. Oxidation corresponds to loss of electrons, while reduction corresponds to gain of electrons.
ExplanationC: Redox chemistry specifically involves changes in electron distribution or oxidation state.
ExplanationD: Neutron gain is a nuclear process and does not define chemical oxidation.

Question: Which molecule carries hereditary information in most living organisms?
ExplanationA: Correct. DNA stores hereditary information in most living organisms through its nucleotide sequence.
ExplanationB: ATP is primarily an energy-transfer molecule rather than the main hereditary material.
ExplanationC: Glucose is an important metabolic fuel and is not the principal genetic material.
ExplanationD: Cholesterol is a lipid important in membranes and hormone synthesis, not hereditary information storage.

Question: Insulin is secreted mainly by which cells of the pancreas?
ExplanationA: Pancreatic alpha cells mainly secrete glucagon.
ExplanationB: Correct. Beta cells in the islets of Langerhans secrete insulin.
ExplanationC: Red blood cells transport respiratory gases and do not secrete insulin.
ExplanationD: Neurons transmit nerve signals and are not the pancreatic source of insulin.

Question: What is the basic structural and functional unit of the human kidney?
ExplanationA: A neuron is a functional cell of the nervous system.
ExplanationB: An alveolus is a tiny air sac involved in gas exchange in the lungs.
ExplanationC: Correct. The nephron filters blood and performs the core urine-forming functions of the kidney.
ExplanationD: A villus is a projection of the small intestine that aids nutrient absorption.

Question: A major purpose of vaccination is to:
OptionA: Create immunological memory against a specific pathogen or antigen
OptionB: Destroy all microorganisms in the body permanently
ExplanationA: Correct. Vaccination exposes the immune system safely to antigenic material so that memory cells and a faster future response can develop.
ExplanationB: Vaccines do not permanently destroy every microorganism in the body.
ExplanationC: Vaccination does not function by replacing red blood cells.
ExplanationD: Continuous fever is not the objective of vaccination.

Question: A geostationary satellite must have an orbital period approximately equal to:
ExplanationA: About 90 minutes is typical of many low-Earth-orbit satellites, not geostationary orbit.
ExplanationB: A six-hour period would not keep a satellite fixed over one longitude.
ExplanationC: A twelve-hour period is associated with some navigation orbits, not geostationary orbit.
ExplanationD: Correct. A geostationary satellite has an orbital period equal to Earth's rotation period, approximately 24 hours, and orbits above the equator in the same direction as Earth's rotation.

Question: Approximately what is Earth's escape velocity from the surface, neglecting atmospheric resistance?
ExplanationA: 1.1 km/s is far below Earth's escape velocity.
ExplanationB: 5.6 km/s is about half the standard approximate escape velocity from Earth.
ExplanationC: Correct. Earth's escape velocity from the surface is approximately 11.2 km/s.
ExplanationD: 22.4 km/s is about twice the standard approximate value.

Question: Which element is widely used as the base semiconductor material in conventional electronic chips?
ExplanationA: Copper is an excellent conductor but is not the standard base semiconductor material for most conventional chips.
ExplanationB: Correct. Silicon is a semiconductor whose electrical properties can be controlled through doping and fabrication.
ExplanationC: Sodium is a highly reactive metal and is not the conventional chip substrate.
ExplanationD: Argon is a noble gas and is not a semiconductor substrate.

Question: How many bits are used in an IPv4 address?
ExplanationA: Sixteen bits are insufficient for the standard IPv4 address format.
ExplanationB: Correct. IPv4 uses 32-bit addresses, conventionally written as four decimal octets.
ExplanationC: Sixty-four bits is not the IPv4 address length.
ExplanationD: IPv6 uses 128-bit addresses, not IPv4.

Question: Which statement best describes machine learning?
OptionA: It is a subset of artificial intelligence in which systems learn patterns from data
OptionB: It is only the physical manufacture of computer chips
OptionC: It is another name for computer networking cables
OptionD: It requires no data or examples under any circumstances
ExplanationA: Correct. Machine learning is a branch of AI that develops models able to learn patterns or relationships from data or experience.
ExplanationB: Chip fabrication is semiconductor manufacturing, not machine learning.
ExplanationC: Networking hardware and cabling are not equivalent to machine learning.
ExplanationD: Machine-learning systems generally depend on data, examples, rewards, simulations or other forms of experience.

Question: Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR) is primarily used to:
OptionC: Convert proteins directly into DNA in cells
ExplanationA: Correct. PCR repeatedly copies a target DNA region, producing many copies for analysis or downstream use.
ExplanationB: Atmospheric pressure is measured with instruments such as barometers, not PCR.
ExplanationC: PCR amplifies DNA templates; it does not generally convert proteins directly into DNA.
ExplanationD: Planetary mass classification is unrelated to PCR.

Question: In the food chain grass → grasshopper → frog, grass contains 10,000 kJ of energy. Assuming exactly 10% is transferred at each step, how much energy reaches the frog?
ExplanationA: 10 kJ would follow three transfers: 10,000 × 0.1 × 0.1 × 0.1. The frog is reached after only two transfers.
ExplanationB: The grasshopper receives 10,000 × 0.1 = 1,000 kJ, and the frog receives 1,000 × 0.1 = 100 kJ.
ExplanationC: 1,000 kJ is the energy reaching the grasshopper after one transfer. A second transfer reduces the frog's share to 100 kJ.
ExplanationD: 10,000 kJ is the starting energy in grass. Keeping this amount at the frog level ignores both transfers and their energy losses.

Question: In an aquatic food chain where methylmercury biomagnifies, which group generally has the highest methylmercury concentration?
OptionD: Large predatory fish feeding on small fish
ExplanationA: Phytoplankton occupy the producer level. They can take up contaminants, but biomagnification increases concentrations further up this food chain.
ExplanationB: Zooplankton can accumulate methylmercury from their food, but they are below both fish groups in the stated food chain.
ExplanationC: Small fish accumulate methylmercury from contaminated prey, but larger fish that repeatedly consume them generally reach higher concentrations.
ExplanationD: Large predatory fish accumulate methylmercury from many contaminated prey. Their high trophic position and often long lifespan favour high concentrations.

Question: Excess input of which pair of nutrients most commonly drives eutrophication in lakes and coastal waters?
ExplanationA: Excess nitrogen and phosphorus encourage algal blooms. Respiration and decomposition of the resulting organic matter can deplete dissolved oxygen and harm aquatic animals.
ExplanationB: Sodium and chloride mainly affect salinity. They are not the principal nutrient pair responsible for typical eutrophication.
ExplanationC: Calcium and magnesium are major contributors to water hardness. Excess nitrogen and phosphorus are the main nutrient drivers of eutrophication.
ExplanationD: Iron and zinc are needed in small amounts by organisms, but they are not the principal pair associated with widespread nutrient pollution.

Question: The stratospheric ozone layer protects life mainly by absorbing much of which incoming solar radiation?
ExplanationA: Radio waves have much longer wavelengths than ultraviolet radiation. Absorbing them is not the ozone layer's main protective role.
ExplanationB: Much visible sunlight reaches Earth's surface and supports photosynthesis. The ozone layer does not provide protection mainly by blocking visible light.
ExplanationC: Ozone absorbs most incoming UV-B, reducing radiation that can damage DNA and living tissues. Some UV-B still reaches Earth's surface.
ExplanationD: Microwaves have longer wavelengths than visible and ultraviolet radiation. Blocking them is not the ozone layer's main protective function.

Question: Which action is an example of in-situ conservation of a wild species?
OptionA: Storing its seeds in a seed bank
OptionB: Protecting its wild population in its natural habitat
OptionC: Breeding it in a zoo outside its natural habitat
OptionD: Maintaining its tissues in a laboratory collection
ExplanationA: A seed bank preserves genetic material away from the species' natural habitat, so it is an ex-situ conservation method.
ExplanationB: Protecting a species where it naturally lives maintains its population within its ecosystem. This is in-situ conservation.
ExplanationC: Zoo breeding outside the natural habitat is ex-situ conservation, even when it supports later reintroduction into the wild.
ExplanationD: A laboratory tissue collection preserves biological material outside the natural habitat and is therefore an ex-situ approach.

Question: The Ramsar Convention, adopted in 1971, was established primarily for the conservation of which ecosystems?
OptionC: Hot deserts and shifting sand dunes
OptionD: Wetlands such as marshes, lakes and peatlands
ExplanationA: Dry grasslands and savannas support important biodiversity, but they are not the defining ecosystem focus of the Ramsar Convention.
ExplanationB: Glaciers and snowfields are important water stores, but the Ramsar Convention was established specifically around wetland conservation.
ExplanationC: Hot deserts and sand dunes have distinct conservation needs. They are not the central ecosystem category addressed by Ramsar.
ExplanationD: The Convention concerns wetlands and their habitats, including those supporting waterfowl. It was adopted on 2 February 1971 in Ramsar, Iran.

Question: Which description best identifies an invasive alien species?
OptionA: A species introduced outside its natural range whose spread threatens biodiversity
OptionB: Any native species whose population increases rapidly
OptionC: Every introduced species, regardless of its ecological effects
OptionD: Any rare species restricted to a small geographical area
ExplanationA: An invasive alien species occurs outside its natural distribution through introduction, and its introduction or spread threatens biological diversity.
ExplanationB: A native species does not become alien merely because its population grows. Origin outside the natural range is part of the definition.
ExplanationC: Many introduced species do not become invasive. Introduction alone is insufficient; a threat to biodiversity distinguishes invasive alien species.
ExplanationD: A species restricted to a particular area may be endemic. Rarity or a small range does not by itself establish alien origin or invasiveness.

Question: Which of the following gases contributes significantly to Earth's natural greenhouse effect?
ExplanationA: Nitrogen makes up most of the atmosphere, but molecular nitrogen is not a major direct absorber of Earth's outgoing infrared radiation.
ExplanationB: Oxygen is essential for aerobic life, but molecular oxygen is not a major direct greenhouse gas.
ExplanationC: Carbon dioxide absorbs and re-emits infrared radiation, slowing the escape of energy to space and warming the lower atmosphere and surface.
ExplanationD: Argon is a monatomic noble gas and is not a major direct greenhouse gas. Its atmospheric abundance does not imply strong infrared absorption.

Question: Which process is carried out by Rhizobium bacteria living in the root nodules of legumes?
ExplanationA: Nitrification converts ammonium into nitrite and then nitrate. It is distinct from the atmospheric nitrogen conversion performed in legume nodules.
ExplanationB: Rhizobium converts atmospheric nitrogen into biologically usable nitrogen compounds in association with legumes. This symbiotic process is nitrogen fixation.
ExplanationC: Denitrification converts nitrate into gaseous nitrogen, returning nitrogen to the atmosphere rather than supplying newly fixed nitrogen to legumes.
ExplanationD: Ammonification releases ammonium from organic nitrogen in wastes and dead matter. It does not begin with atmospheric nitrogen gas.

Question: Which habitat is most characteristic of mangrove forests?
OptionB: Cold alpine slopes above the tree line
OptionC: Dry desert interiors far from the coast
OptionD: Temperate inland grasslands without tidal flooding
ExplanationA: Mangroves are adapted to coastal intertidal conditions, including tidal flooding and oxygen-poor soils, mainly in tropical and subtropical regions.
ExplanationB: Cold alpine slopes experience freezing conditions and lack coastal tides. They do not provide the warm intertidal setting typical of mangroves.
ExplanationC: Dry desert interiors lack the regular tidal water supply characteristic of mangrove habitats. Mangrove adaptations address coastal conditions rather than inland aridity.
ExplanationD: Temperate inland grasslands lack tidal flooding and the coastal setting of mangrove forests. Mangroves typically grow in warmer intertidal areas.

Question: The ozone layer that absorbs much of the Sun's harmful ultraviolet radiation is concentrated mainly in the:
ExplanationA: Incorrect. The troposphere is the lowest atmospheric layer where most weather occurs.
ExplanationB: Correct. Most atmospheric ozone is concentrated in the stratosphere.
ExplanationC: Incorrect. The mesosphere lies above the stratosphere.
ExplanationD: Incorrect. The thermosphere is much higher and is not where the ozone layer is concentrated.

Question: ORV Sagar Manthan, whose launch was announced on 9 September 2026, is which type of platform?
ExplanationA: A submarine operates underwater; Sagar Manthan was announced as an ocean research vessel.
ExplanationB: Sagar Manthan is an Ocean Research Vessel intended for marine scientific work.
ExplanationC: A maritime patrol aircraft is airborne; Sagar Manthan is a ship.
ExplanationD: A communications satellite operates in space; this announcement concerns a research vessel.

Question: Which body announced an Aadhaar Face Authentication SDK and Sandbox at Global Fintech Fest 2026 on 9 September?
OptionB: Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)
ExplanationA: RBI is India's central bank; this Aadhaar authentication announcement came from UIDAI.
ExplanationB: SEBI regulates securities markets; the announced tools relate to Aadhaar authentication.
ExplanationC: NPCI operates retail payment systems; UIDAI introduced these Aadhaar authentication tools.
ExplanationD: UIDAI administers Aadhaar and announced both the SDK and the Sandbox.

Question: WHO's QIRA user manual, published on 8 September 2026, supports which main activity?
OptionA: Rapid risk assessment of acute public-health events
OptionB: Population estimates based solely on census records
OptionC: Commercial approval of every new medicine
OptionD: Individual diagnosis and prescription of medicines
ExplanationA: QIRA means Quick and Immediate Risk Assessment. It helps assess verified public-health signals or events and identify initial response actions.
ExplanationB: Census-based population estimation is a demographic activity. QIRA assesses immediate risks associated with acute public-health events.
ExplanationC: Regulatory approval evaluates medicines for market use. The QIRA manual instead supports public-health intelligence and initial risk assessment.
ExplanationD: The tool supports event-level public-health decisions. It is not a system for diagnosing individual patients or prescribing their medicines.

Question: As scheduled on 10 September 2026, which country will host the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games beginning on 19 September 2026?
ExplanationA: China hosted the previous edition in Hangzhou. Aichi-Nagoya is the designated Japanese host area for the 2026 Games.
ExplanationB: South Korea is not the country containing Aichi Prefecture or Nagoya City. The scheduled 2026 host is Japan.
ExplanationC: Aichi Prefecture and Nagoya City are in Japan. The Games are scheduled for 19 September to 4 October 2026.
ExplanationD: Indonesia hosted the 2018 edition in Jakarta and Palembang. The 2026 host locations are Aichi and Nagoya in Japan.

Question: Which city hosted UNCCD COP17, whose closing statement UNEP issued on 29 August 2026?
ExplanationA: Geneva is an important centre for international diplomacy, but the COP17 closing statement identifies Ulaanbaatar as its location.
ExplanationB: Bonn is associated with the UNCCD secretariat. The 2026 COP17 meeting itself was held in Ulaanbaatar.
ExplanationC: Nairobi is the headquarters city of UNEP. UNEP's statement on these talks was issued for the meeting in Mongolia.
ExplanationD: UNEP identifies Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia, as the location of the COP17 closing statement. The talks addressed land restoration and drought.

Question: The Chennai Declaration announced at the BRICS ministerial meeting on 22 August 2026 primarily concerned which area?
OptionB: The launch of a single BRICS currency
OptionD: A common passport for all BRICS citizens
ExplanationA: The declaration came from the 14th BRICS Science Ministerial Meeting. It emphasised research cooperation, shared infrastructure and opportunities for scientists and innovators.
ExplanationB: A single currency would be a monetary integration measure. The Chennai Declaration concerned science, technology and innovation cooperation.
ExplanationC: A mutual-defence treaty would establish military commitments. The reported declaration focused on scientific collaboration and sustainable development.
ExplanationD: A common passport would concern citizenship and travel arrangements. The declaration instead addressed research networks, innovation and scientific talent.

Question: According to the official February 2026 briefing, which three pillars framed the India AI Impact Summit 2026?
ExplanationA: These are technology and infrastructure terms. They were not the three overarching pillars named in the official summit briefing.
ExplanationB: These terms describe trade and fiscal policy. The summit's named pillars focused on people, planetary sustainability and progress.
ExplanationC: The official briefing names People, Planet and Progress, covering areas such as skilling, sustainable AI and economic and social development.
ExplanationD: These are security and foreign-policy concepts. They were not the three pillars set out for the AI Impact Summit.

Question: The BBNJ Agreement entered into force on 17 January 2026. What is its central subject?
OptionA: Biodiversity solely within terrestrial national parks
OptionC: Air pollution from international passenger aircraft
OptionD: Domestic tariffs on retail fish sales
ExplanationA: Terrestrial national parks lie outside this agreement's marine focus. BBNJ addresses biodiversity in areas beyond national jurisdiction.
ExplanationB: The agreement concerns conservation and sustainable use of marine biodiversity beyond national jurisdiction, including protected areas, genetic resources and environmental assessments.
ExplanationC: Aircraft emissions are an aviation and climate-policy issue. They are not the central subject of this agreement under the law of the sea.
ExplanationD: The agreement is not principally a domestic fish-tax measure. Its focus is marine biodiversity, international cooperation and related conservation tools.

Question: Which country hosted the official global commemoration of World Environment Day on 5 June 2026?
ExplanationA: World Environment Day is observed globally, but the 2026 official commemoration identified by UNEP was held in Baku, not in India.
ExplanationB: Brazil's participation in international environmental diplomacy does not make it the host of this event; the 2026 commemoration was in Azerbaijan.
ExplanationC: UNEP is headquartered in Kenya, but its headquarters location is distinct from the 2026 official host country.
ExplanationD: UNEP's 5 June 2026 release confirms that Azerbaijan hosted the official commemoration in Baku, with climate action as the year's focus.

Question: With which bloc did India conclude negotiations for a Free Trade Agreement on 27 January 2026, according to the European Commission?
ExplanationA: The European Commission records that EU-India FTA negotiations concluded on 27 January 2026. Concluding negotiations is distinct from the agreement entering into force.
ExplanationB: EFTA is a separate grouping from the EU. The European Commission's 27 January announcement concerned the European Union.
ExplanationC: ASEAN is a Southeast Asian regional grouping. It was not the counterpart in the European Commission's January 2026 announcement.
ExplanationD: The GCC groups Gulf Arab states. The specified negotiation milestone concerned India and the European Union.

Question: Keezhadi (Keeladi), the archaeological settlement near Madurai, is associated with which river valley?
ExplanationA: The Cauvery valley includes the delta and the ancient port of Poompuhar. Keezhadi belongs to a different river valley near Madurai.
ExplanationB: Keezhadi is an early historic settlement in the Vaigai valley near Madurai. Its excavations provide evidence of settlement, crafts and everyday life in ancient Tamil society.
ExplanationC: The Palar is associated with northern Tamil Nadu. It is not the river valley in which the Keezhadi settlement is located.
ExplanationD: The Tamirabarani flows through the Tirunelveli region farther south. Keezhadi is associated with the Vaigai valley.

Question: In which year did the official name of Madras State change to Tamil Nadu?
ExplanationA: 1947 marks Indian independence. The name Tamil Nadu did not replace Madras State at that time.
ExplanationB: The 1956 reorganisation changed state boundaries on linguistic lines. The state continued to be called Madras after that reorganisation.
ExplanationC: The state legislature passed a resolution seeking the name Tamil Nadu in July 1967. The formal name change took effect later.
ExplanationD: The name Tamil Nadu took effect on 14 January 1969. Distinguish this from the legislature's resolution passed in 1967.

Question: The rock-cut monuments and Shore Temple at Mamallapuram (Mahabalipuram) are chiefly associated with which dynasty?
ExplanationA: Pallava rulers developed Mamallapuram's cave temples, monolithic rathas and structural temples. UNESCO identifies this group of monuments with Pallava civilisation.
ExplanationB: The Cholas are associated with the Great Living Chola Temples, including the Brihadisvara Temple at Thanjavur. Mamallapuram's famous monument group is Pallava.
ExplanationC: The Hoysalas are associated with ornate temples at places such as Belur and Halebidu in Karnataka. They did not create Mamallapuram's Pallava monument group.
ExplanationD: Vijayanagara rulers are strongly associated with Hampi and later temple expansion in southern India. Mamallapuram's principal monuments belong to an earlier Pallava period.

Question: Who founded the Swadeshi Steam Navigation Company in 1906 to challenge British dominance in shipping?
ExplanationA: Subramania Bharati promoted nationalism through poetry and journalism and supported Swadeshi causes. The shipping company's founder was V. O. Chidambaram Pillai.
ExplanationB: Subramania Siva helped spread nationalist ideas through speeches and activism. V. O. Chidambaram Pillai established the Swadeshi Steam Navigation Company.
ExplanationC: V. O. Chidambaram Pillai founded the company in 1906. Its Tuticorin–Colombo service challenged the British India Steam Navigation Company and put Swadeshi ideas into business practice.
ExplanationD: C. Rajagopalachari led the Vedaranyam Salt March in 1930. The Swadeshi shipping enterprise of 1906 was founded by V. O. Chidambaram Pillai.

Question: In which year did the Vellore sepoy uprising occur?
ExplanationA: 1757 is associated with the Battle of Plassey in Bengal. The uprising inside Vellore Fort occurred several decades later.
ExplanationB: The Vellore uprising took place in 1806, when sepoys rose against British authority inside the fort. It preceded the wider Revolt of 1857.
ExplanationC: 1857 marks the much wider uprising against East India Company rule. The Vellore uprising was a separate, earlier event in 1806.
ExplanationD: 1942 is associated with the Quit India Movement. The Vellore sepoy uprising occurred during the earlier period of East India Company rule.

Question: Which set names the three principal divisions of the Thirukkural?
ExplanationA: Aram, Porul and Inbam are the Thirukkural's three divisions, dealing broadly with virtue, wealth and public life, and love. The work contains 1,330 couplets.
ExplanationB: Iyal, Isai and Nadagam refer to the threefold Tamil tradition of literature, music and drama. They are not the divisions of the Thirukkural.
ExplanationC: Kurinji, Mullai and Marutham are three of the five landscape categories used in classical Tamil poetry. They do not name the Thirukkural's divisions.
ExplanationD: Chera, Chola and Pandya name the three major ancient Tamil royal dynasties. They are political names, not divisions of the Thirukkural.

Question: The ancient port of Poompuhar lies near the mouth of which river?
ExplanationA: The Palar reaches the coast farther north in Tamil Nadu. Poompuhar is associated with the Cauvery river mouth.
ExplanationB: The Vaigai is associated with Madurai and flows east through southern Tamil Nadu. It is not the river at the port of Kaveripoompattinam.
ExplanationC: The Tamirabarani drains the Tirunelveli region and reaches the Gulf of Mannar. Poompuhar lies farther north near the Cauvery mouth.
ExplanationD: Poompuhar is located near the mouth of the Cauvery, also spelled Kaveri. Its older name, Kaveripoompattinam, reflects this river association.

Question: Which habitat is especially important for conserving the Nilgiri tahr in Tamil Nadu?
OptionC: High-altitude grasslands of the Western Ghats
ExplanationA: Mangroves grow in tidal coastal environments. Nilgiri tahr conservation centres on mountain habitats in the Western Ghats.
ExplanationB: Desert dunes are arid sandy habitats. They do not represent the high-altitude Western Ghats grasslands used by the Nilgiri tahr.
ExplanationC: High-altitude grasslands within the Western Ghats' shola–grassland landscape provide crucial Nilgiri tahr habitat. Protecting and restoring these grasslands supports conservation.
ExplanationD: Himalayan alpine meadows are mountain habitats, but they are in a different mountain system. The Nilgiri tahr is associated with the Western Ghats.

Question: Which Indian classical dance form is most closely associated with Tamil Nadu?
ExplanationA: Odissi is associated with Odisha and its temple and performance traditions. It is a different classical dance form from Tamil Nadu's Bharatanatyam.
ExplanationB: Bharatanatyam developed from Tamil Nadu's temple dance tradition. It combines rhythmic movement with expressive gestures and facial expression.
ExplanationC: Kathakali is a dance-drama tradition associated with Kerala, known for elaborate costumes and makeup. It is distinct from Bharatanatyam.
ExplanationD: Sattriya developed in Assam's Vaishnavite monastery tradition. Its regional and institutional origins differ from those of Bharatanatyam.

Question: The fort built at Tharangambadi (Tranquebar) in 1620 is associated with which European power?
ExplanationA: The Portuguese established settlements at several Indian ports, including Goa. The 1620 fort at Tharangambadi is associated with the Danes.
ExplanationB: The Dutch had important trading settlements such as Pulicat. Tharangambadi's fort belongs to the Danish trading settlement.
ExplanationC: The French are associated with settlements such as Puducherry. The fort at Tharangambadi was established by the Danes.
ExplanationD: The Danes built the fort at Tharangambadi in 1620. The surviving fort and other buildings reflect the town's Danish trading history.

Question: A price rises by 20% and then falls by 20% of the increased price. What is the overall change from the original price?
ExplanationA: The two percentages use different bases. Starting at ₹100, the rise gives ₹120 and the fall removes ₹24, so the price does not return to ₹100.
ExplanationB: Take the original price as ₹100. After the rise it is ₹120; after the fall it is ₹120 × 0.80 = ₹96. The overall decrease is 4%.
ExplanationC: A 4% increase would produce ₹104 from ₹100. The actual multiplier is 1.20 × 0.80 = 0.96, which produces ₹96.
ExplanationD: An 8% decrease would produce ₹92 from ₹100. The actual reduction from the original price is ₹100 − ₹96 = ₹4, so the decrease is 4%.

Subtopic: Ratio and proportion — transfer of money
Question: Arun and Bala have money in the ratio 3:5. Bala gives ₹200 to Arun, after which they have equal amounts. What was their combined total?
ExplanationA: With a total of ₹800, the initial amounts would be ₹300 and ₹500. After the transfer they would be ₹500 and ₹300, which are unequal.
ExplanationB: With a total of ₹1,200, the initial amounts would be ₹450 and ₹750. After the transfer they would be ₹650 and ₹550, which are unequal.
ExplanationC: With a total of ₹2,000, the initial amounts would be ₹750 and ₹1,250. After the transfer they would be ₹950 and ₹1,050, which are unequal.
ExplanationD: Let the amounts be 3x and 5x. Then 3x + 200 = 5x − 200, so x = 200. Their total is 8x = ₹1,600; both have ₹800 after the transfer.

Question: In the same test, 20 students have an average score of 60 marks and another 30 students have an average of 70 marks. What is the average for all 50 students?
ExplanationA: The total score is 20 × 60 + 30 × 70 = 3,300 marks. Divide by 50 students: 3,300 ÷ 50 = 66 marks.
ExplanationB: 65 is the simple average of 60 and 70. The groups have different sizes, so their averages must be weighted by 20 and 30 students.
ExplanationC: 64 results from reversing the group sizes: (30 × 60 + 20 × 70) ÷ 50. The 70-mark average belongs to the larger, 30-student group.
ExplanationD: An average of 68 would require 50 × 68 = 3,400 total marks. The two groups actually contribute 1,200 + 2,100 = 3,300 marks.

Subtopic: Profit and loss — markup and discount
Question: A shopkeeper marks an item 25% above its cost price, then offers a 10% discount on the marked price. What is the profit percentage on cost price?
ExplanationA: Subtracting 10 from 25 gives 15, but the percentages have different bases. For a ₹100 cost, the discount is 10% of ₹125, or ₹12.50.
ExplanationB: 10% is the discount on marked price, not the profit on cost. A ₹100 item sells for ₹125 − ₹12.50 = ₹112.50.
ExplanationC: Take cost price as ₹100. Marked price is ₹125 and selling price is ₹125 × 0.90 = ₹112.50. Profit is ₹12.50 on ₹100, or 12.5%.

Question: பின்வருவனவற்றுள் குறில் உயிரெழுத்து எது?

ExplanationB: ‘ஆ’ நெடில் உயிரெழுத்து. ‘அ’ குறில்; அதனுடன் தொடர்புடைய ‘ஆ’ நெடில்.
ExplanationC: ‘இ’ குறில் உயிரெழுத்து. அ, இ, உ, எ, ஒ ஆகிய ஐந்தும் குறில் உயிரெழுத்துகள்; இவற்றின் இயல்பான ஒலிப்பளவு ஒரு மாத்திரை.
ExplanationD: ‘ஓ’ நெடில் உயிரெழுத்து. ‘ஒ’ குறில்; ‘ஓ’ நெடில் என்பதால் இரண்டையும் வேறுபடுத்த வேண்டும்.

Question: பின்வரும் மெய்யெழுத்துகளில் மெல்லினத்தைச் சேர்ந்தது எது?

ExplanationB: ‘ங்’ மெல்லின மெய்யெழுத்து. ங், ஞ், ண், ந், ம், ன் ஆகிய ஆறும் மெல்லின எழுத்துகள்.
ExplanationC: ‘ய்’ இடையின மெய்யெழுத்து. ய், ர், ல், வ், ழ், ள் ஆகியவை இடையின எழுத்துகள்.
ExplanationD: ‘ர்’ இடையினத்தைச் சேர்ந்தது. ‘ர்’ மற்றும் ‘ற்’ வெவ்வேறு எழுத்துகள்; ‘ற்’ வல்லினத்தைச் சேர்ந்தது.

Question: தமிழில் 12 உயிரெழுத்துகளும் 18 மெய்யெழுத்துகளும் இணைவதால் உருவாகும் உயிர்மெய்யெழுத்துகளின் எண்ணிக்கை என்ன?

ExplanationB: 18 என்பது மெய்யெழுத்துகளின் எண்ணிக்கை. ஒவ்வொரு மெய்யும் பல உயிர்மெய் வடிவங்களை உருவாக்குவதால் 18 மட்டும் விடையாகாது.
ExplanationC: 247 என்பது 12 உயிர், 18 மெய், 216 உயிர்மெய், ஓர் ஆய்தம் ஆகியவற்றின் மொத்த எண்ணிக்கை. இங்கு உயிர்மெய்யெழுத்துகள் மட்டும் கேட்கப்பட்டுள்ளன.
ExplanationD: 18 மெய்யெழுத்துகளில் ஒவ்வொன்றும் 12 உயிரெழுத்துகளுடன் இணையும். எனவே 18 × 12 = 216 உயிர்மெய்யெழுத்துகள் உருவாகின்றன.

Question: பின்வரும் பெயர்ச்சொற்களில் காலப்பெயர் எது?
ExplanationA: ‘காலை’ ஒரு பொழுதைக் குறிக்கிறது. பொழுது, நாள், மாதம் போன்ற காலப் பகுதிகளின் பெயர்கள் காலப்பெயர்கள் ஆகும்.
ExplanationB: ‘சென்னை’ ஓர் ஊரின் பெயர். இடத்தைக் குறிப்பதால் இது இடப்பெயர் ஆகும்.
ExplanationC: ‘மரம்’ ஓர் உயிருள்ள பொருளைக் குறிக்கிறது. எனவே இது பொருட்பெயர் வகையைச் சேர்ந்தது.
ExplanationD: ‘வெண்மை’ ஒரு நிறப் பண்பைக் குறிக்கிறது. எனவே இது பண்புப்பெயர் ஆகும்.

Question: ‘கண்ணன் பாடி மகிழ்ந்தான்’ என்ற தொடரில் ‘பாடி’ என்பதன் இலக்கண வகை எது?
ExplanationA: பெயரெச்சம் ஒரு பெயர்ச்சொல்லைக் கொண்டு முடியும். ‘பாடிய சிறுவன்’ என்பதில் ‘பாடிய’ பெயரெச்சம்; கொடுக்கப்பட்ட தொடரில் ‘பாடி’ வினைச்சொல்லைத் தழுவுகிறது.
ExplanationB: வினைமுற்று ஒரு செயலை முழுமையாக உணர்த்தும். இத்தொடரில் ‘மகிழ்ந்தான்’ வினைமுற்று; ‘பாடி’ தனித்து வினைமுற்றாக அமையவில்லை.
ExplanationC: பெயர்ச்சொல் ஒரு பொருள், இடம் போன்றவற்றின் பெயராக வரும். இங்கு ‘பாடி’ பெயராக வராமல் பாடுதல் என்னும் செயலைக் குறிக்கிறது.
ExplanationD: ‘பாடி’ என்பது ‘மகிழ்ந்தான்’ என்ற வினைமுற்றைக் கொண்டு முடிகிறது. இவ்வாறு வினைச்சொல்லைக் கொண்டு முடியும் எச்சம் வினையெச்சம் ஆகும்.

Question: ‘மாணவன் புத்தகத்தைப் படித்தான்’ என்ற தொடரில் ‘புத்தகத்தை’ என்பதில் வந்துள்ள ‘ஐ’ எந்த வேற்றுமையின் உருபு?
ExplanationA: மூன்றாம் வேற்றுமைக்குரிய உருபுகளில் ‘ஆல்’ ஒன்று; அது கருவிப்பொருள் போன்ற பொருள்களில் வரும். இங்கு வந்திருப்பது ‘ஆல்’ அல்ல, ‘ஐ’.
ExplanationB: ‘ஐ’ இரண்டாம் வேற்றுமை உருபு. படித்தல் என்னும் செயலில் புத்தகம் செயப்படுபொருளாக இருப்பதை ‘புத்தகத்தை’ என்ற வடிவம் காட்டுகிறது.
ExplanationC: நான்காம் வேற்றுமையின் உருபு ‘கு’. ‘மாணவனுக்குப் புத்தகம் கொடுத்தான்’ என்பதில் பெறுபவரைக் குறிக்கும் வடிவம் இதற்கு எடுத்துக்காட்டு.
ExplanationD: ஆறாம் வேற்றுமையின் உருபுகளில் ‘அது’ ஒன்று. ‘மாணவனது புத்தகம்’ என்பதில் அது உடைமையைக் குறிக்கும்; கேள்வியில் உள்ள ‘ஐ’ இரண்டாம் வேற்றுமைக்குரியது.

Question: சிலப்பதிகாரத்தின் ஆசிரியர் யார்?
ExplanationA: சிலப்பதிகாரம் இளங்கோ அடிகள் இயற்றிய காப்பியமாகக் கருதப்படுகிறது. கோவலன், கண்ணகி ஆகியோரின் வாழ்க்கை அதன் மையக் கதையாக அமைகிறது.
ExplanationB: சீத்தலைச் சாத்தனார் மணிமேகலையின் ஆசிரியர். மணிமேகலை சிலப்பதிகாரத்துடன் தொடர்புடைய காப்பியம் என்றாலும் இரண்டின் ஆசிரியர்களும் வேறுபடுகின்றனர்.
ExplanationC: கம்பர் கம்பராமாயணத்தை இயற்றியவர். சிலப்பதிகாரத்தின் ஆசிரியர் இளங்கோ அடிகள்.
ExplanationD: திருவள்ளுவர் திருக்குறளின் ஆசிரியர். சிலப்பதிகாரம் அவருடைய படைப்பு அல்ல.

Question: பின்வரும் நூல்களில் எட்டுத்தொகையைச் சேர்ந்தது எது?
ExplanationA: திருக்குறள் பதினெண்கீழ்க்கணக்கு நூல்களில் ஒன்று. அது எட்டுத்தொகை நூல்களின் பட்டியலில் இடம்பெறாது.
ExplanationB: சிலப்பதிகாரம் ஐம்பெருங்காப்பியங்களில் ஒன்று. காப்பியத் தொகுப்பையும் எட்டுத்தொகையையும் வேறுபடுத்தி அறிய வேண்டும்.
ExplanationC: நற்றிணை எட்டுத்தொகை நூல்களில் ஒன்று. அது அகப்பொருள் சார்ந்த பாடல்களைக் கொண்ட நூல்.
ExplanationD: சீவகசிந்தாமணி ஐம்பெருங்காப்பியங்களில் ஒன்று. அது எட்டுத்தொகையைச் சேர்ந்த நூல் அல்ல.

Question: ‘கற்றது கைம்மண்ணளவு; கல்லாதது உலகளவு’ என்ற கூற்றின் பொருளைச் சரியாக விளக்குவது எது?
OptionA: கற்றறிந்த அறிவை மட்டுமே நம்பி வாழ வேண்டும்.
OptionB: அதிக நூல்களைப் படித்தவர்களுக்குக் கற்க வேண்டியது எதுவும் இல்லை.
OptionC: நிலத்தின் அளவை அறிவதே கல்வியின் முதன்மை நோக்கம்.
OptionD: நாம் கற்றது சிறிது; இன்னும் கற்க வேண்டியது மிகுதி.
ExplanationA: கற்ற அறிவு மட்டும் போதும் என்று இக்கூற்று சொல்லவில்லை. அறியாதவை அதிகம் என்பதை ‘கல்லாதது உலகளவு’ என்ற பகுதி வலியுறுத்துகிறது.
ExplanationB: எவ்வளவு கற்றிருந்தாலும் கற்க வேண்டியவை மிகுதியாக உள்ளன என்பதே கருத்து. எல்லாவற்றையும் அறிந்துவிட்டதாகக் கருதுவது இதற்கு முரணானது.
ExplanationC: கைம்மண்ணும் உலகமும் அறிவின் அளவை ஒப்பிட்டுக் காட்டும் உவமைகளாக வருகின்றன. நிலத்தின் பரப்பளவை அளப்பது பற்றிய அறிவுரை இது அல்ல.
ExplanationD: கைம்மண்ணளவு என்பது சிறிய அளவையும் உலகளவு என்பது மிகப் பெரிய அளவையும் உணர்த்துகிறது. கற்றது குறைவு, கற்க வேண்டியது அதிகம் என்பதை இவ்வொப்புமை விளக்குகிறது.

Question:
பின்வரும் உரைப்பகுதியைப் படித்து விடையளிக்கவும்:

‘ஒரு பள்ளியில் மரக்கன்றுகள் நடப்பட்டன. மாணவர்கள் குழுக்களாகப் பிரிந்து மாறிமாறி நீர் ஊற்றினர். விடுமுறை நாட்களிலும் பராமரிப்பதற்கான அட்டவணை தயாரிக்கப்பட்டது. மூன்று மாதங்களுக்குப் பிறகு பெரும்பாலான மரக்கன்றுகள் நன்கு வளர்ந்திருந்தன.’

உரைப்பகுதியின் அடிப்படையில் மரக்கன்றுகளின் வளர்ச்சிக்கு உதவியதாக எந்தக் கருத்தை நியாயமாக ஊகிக்கலாம்?
OptionA: தொடர்ந்த பராமரிப்பும் மாணவர்களின் கூட்டு முயற்சியும் உதவின.
OptionB: மாணவர்களின் உதவியின்றி மழை மட்டுமே மரக்கன்றுகளை வளர்த்தது.
OptionC: நடப்பட்ட நாளில் மட்டும் நீர் ஊற்றியது வளர்ச்சிக்குப் போதுமானதாக இருந்தது.
OptionD: ஒவ்வொரு மரக்கன்றுக்கும் தினமும் உரமிட்டதே வளர்ச்சிக்குக் காரணம்.
ExplanationA: குழுக்களாக நீர் ஊற்றியதும் விடுமுறை நாட்களுக்கும் பராமரிப்பு ஏற்பாடு செய்ததும் உரையில் கூறப்பட்டுள்ளன. இவை தொடர்ந்த கவனிப்பும் கூட்டு முயற்சியும் வளர்ச்சிக்கு உதவியதாக ஊகிக்க ஆதரவளிக்கின்றன.
ExplanationB: மழை பற்றிய தகவல் உரையில் இல்லை. மாணவர்கள் நீர் ஊற்றியதாகத் தெளிவாகக் கூறப்பட்டுள்ளதால் மழை மட்டுமே காரணம் என்று கூற முடியாது.
ExplanationC: மாணவர்கள் மாறிமாறி நீர் ஊற்றியதுடன் விடுமுறை நாட்களுக்கும் பராமரிப்பைத் திட்டமிட்டனர். நடப்பட்ட நாளில் மட்டும் நீர் ஊற்றினர் என்பது உரைக்கு முரணானது.
ExplanationD: உரமிடுதல் பற்றிய தகவல் உரையில் தரப்படவில்லை. குறிப்பாக தினமும் உரமிட்டதே காரணம் என்று முடிவு செய்ய உரை ஆதாரம் அளிக்கவில்லை.
